title: In 1054, a Star Exploded and Stayed Visible in Daylight for 23 Days

scenes.text: In 1054, people saw an exploding star in broad daylight.
Chinese astronomers recorded it on July 4 and compared it to Venus.
It stayed visible in the daytime sky for about twenty-three days.
At night, people could see it for nearly two years.
The light had traveled sixty-five hundred years. Today it's the Crab Nebula.
Imagine looking up at noon and seeing a second bright star.

description:
In 1054, people saw an exploding star in broad daylight.
It stayed visible by day for about 23 days and by night for nearly two years. Today it is the Crab Nebula.
What would you have thought if you saw it?
first_comment: Bonus: the Crab Nebula is still expanding today. Have you ever seen it through a telescope?
